newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma arrests about 50 members of Suu Kyi's party.
newsitem.headline: Burma arrests about 50 members of Suu Kyi's party.

text.p: Burma's military government has arrested at least 50 senior members of Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD), a senior NLD official said on Wednesday.
"Our members of parliament (MPs) and some of our members are being arrested ahead of the (May) 27th election anniversary," the NLD official told Reuters from Rangoon.

He said the NLD had heard that at least 50 elected MPs or NLD organisers had been detained over the past few days as they headed to the capital to participate in a celebration commemorating the 1990 electoral victory of the party.
Others, mostly from the provinces, had been told to go back home and not attend the celebration at Suu Kyi's residence.
The NLD source said the party expected to hear of more arrests in the next few days.
He said Suu Kyi was fine and in her compound with several NLD members who had arrived in Rangoon. She could not be reached for comment as her telephone line appears to have been cut.
The NLD won a landslide victory in the May 27, 1990 elections but the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) never recognised the poll results.

The arrests were reminiscent of last May when about 261 elected MPs and senior members of the NLD were detained by the government on their way to attend a party congress timed to coincide with the anniversary of the 1990 election win.
Last year the congress was held despite the arrests. At the meeting, Suu Kyi and her party vowed to continue their fight for democracy despite the SLORC's crackdown.
The NLD official said about 200 MPs had been invited to the celebration this year, and about 100 senior NLD party members were also expected to attend.

"Some of those who were about to leave for Rangoon were detained and not allowed to come," he said. "In the Karen State, MPs were asked by the authorities not to move from their houses. They are using different ways to stop them from coming."
He said other MPs reported they were followed on a bus from their homes in northern Burma, and once they arrived in Rangoon were told to return home or they would be arrested.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment on the arrests.

The SLORC said last May it had only detained the NLD members for questioning and that it was holding them temporarily in order to avoid anarchy. It later released most of them, although some were charged and given long prison sentences.
During their detention, many MPs were forced to sign papers saying they would resign from the party, Suu Kyi said.
Last May's meeting was to have been the first time all elected MPs were due to meet the Nobel Peace laureate since she was released from six years of house arrest in July 1995.

In September, the SLORC thwarted another NLD attempt to hold a party congress, arresting up to 800 members and supporters and barricading streets leading to Suu Kyi's house where the meeting was to be held.
The latest series of arrests comes one day after U.S. President Bill Clinton imposed economic sanctions on Burma. The United States is the fourth largest investor in Burma.
Clinton, who announced the sanctions last month, officially imposed the ban on all new U.S. investment in Burma on Tuesday, citing "severe repression" in the country.
The United States and many Western nations have criticised Burma's military rulers of human rights abuses and for failing to recognise the election of the NLD.
